contract.productionCallChain: Existing createPianolaLifecycle -> supervisor start/reconcile -> one pianola watch-scope <scope-id> child per persisted enabled selection -> registered CLI action -> createPianolaScopeWorkerDeps -> runPianolaScopeCycle. Legacy path scopes report an explicit reconfiguration failure instead of falling through to orchestration.
contract.discovery: Each native session census includes every current owner, groupId (string or null), parentSessionId and open AI tab. Polling discovers new tabs/agents and membership/lineage changes without per-tab processes or per-poll inference. Existing explicit watches are retained; future legacy Auto-Watch does not override a matching scope, disabled scope or exclusion.
contract.scheduling: At most 20 changed, ready tabs per serial worker cycle; persisted nextTabIndex rotates over the native census to avoid starvation by failing/active prefixes. Unavailable tab cursors are isolated even on enrollment. Metadata/checkpoint corruption fails closed; native supervisor restart/backoff and health remain in use.
contract.baselineAndRecovery: Existing tab checkpoints are committed before work. Old/new enrollment, ancestry/config binding, paused tabs and ownership changes use existing baseline/dedup logic. A stream busy on enrollment is checked after completion under its original message ID, including unchanged final text. Full transcript fetch plus cursor/identity checks preserves current-turn risk. Scope disable/Encore-off suspends its checkpoint; worker persistence preserves host suspension and admitted intents. Restart after a crash restores durable state.
contract.guardedSend: Worker uses dedicated pianola_scope_reply, with no send_command fallback. Native authenticated CLI admission rechecks Encore, current owner/membership/paused/busy state, configuration/binding, exact recipient/cursor, persisted unresolved intent and current rule/answer. It appends deliveryStatus=admitted to the existing audit and claims the checkpoint before invoking the ordinary renderer send path with an explicit tab, background=true, no force/queue, and requireDeliveryReceipt=true.
contract.deliverySafety: Optional audit deliveryStatus=admitted and checkpoint unresolvedIntent.admitted are backward compatible. The native claim prevents duplicate answers for the same agent/tab/message across overlapping requests. A definitive renderer rejection permits the existing bounded retry; a timeout/malformed receipt/disconnect is unknown and leaves intent/audit claim in place without blind retry. Legacy dispatch receipt behavior is unchanged.
contract.nextDecisionSeam: This increment composes rule answers and existing human escalation only. contract.persistence: Optional validated PianolaDecisionRecord.lifecycle folds intent, manager handoff, escalation, controlled answer, native receipt and observed continuation under one original decision ID. Legacy records remain readable and legacy explicit tab watches retain their prior behavior. The scope worker uses the lifecycle instead of heuristic handoff-resolution attribution. Invalid/oversized lifecycle appends fail before send.
contract.statuses: mira_processing / waiting_human / agent_running / blocked / paused / done, with nextActor and concrete nextAction, original scope/configuration/lineage guard, manager ID/tab, native delivery phase/outcome, source identity/time and observed answer message ID. Source status is separate from installed/runtime acceptance.
contract.nativeAdmission: Rule answer and Mira handoff use pianola_scope_reply; handoffs select and persist an eligible exact manager tab from the configured managerAgentId. Native admission checks current Encore consent, scope selection, overlap ownership, paused/busy state, exact requesting agent/tab/cursor, durable intent and full current-turn risk. Mira receives the complete current turn as untrusted data and uses only the decision-ID resolver to answer.
contract.controlledResolution: pianola resolve <decision-id> --answer <text> or --escalation <recommendation> sends caller agent/tab provenance to registered pianola_decision_resolve. Only the bound manager tab can answer its eligible handoff; sensitive/high-risk answers require explicit human resolution. Native preload pianola.resolveDecision -> gated IPC -> current WebServer transport -> the same resolvePianolaDecision service. The manager CLI cannot choose human provenance, including via generic bridge.invoke.
contract.dedupAndDelivery: Persist answer intent/audit claim synchronously before ordinary background renderer delivery with an explicit target tab, no force and required receipt. Duplicate claims or unknown ANSWER delivery cannot resend; an explicitly rejected answer can be reconsidered through a deliberate human resolution. Unknown JUDGMENT delivery may be reconciled by the assigned manager reply without repeating the handoff. Native accepted delivery is distinct from recipient activity; observation records continuation/completion, and never guesses an unknown answer author. Worker outcomes preserve newer native receipt/actor changes.
contract.pauseAndRecovery: Supervisor suspension and standalone worker disable persist paused decisions without clearing claims. Scope cycles reconcile native receipts/current transcripts after restart, isolate per-tab failures, and preserve unknown sends. Manager deadline moves once to waiting_human; unchanged pending polls do not emit new handoffs/decisions. Membership or recipient loss pauses/blocks the original decision and never redirects it.
contract.provenanceForLearning: Explicit human resolutions carry the acting web user ID, desktop or web-owner identity, group at decision time, source timestamp and observed answer message ID. Manager/rule replies remain distinct; user-role transcript text alone becomes unknown. V2-08 must only consume attributable, settled human records and must not equate anonymous desktop/web-owner identity with Chris without its configured identity policy.
